evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: latest value ~10.5-10.9 mg/L at t=50-52 h (rows idx 250-259), >5x the 2 mg/L limit
Receiving DO trajectory parallels source-1/2/3 trajectories, which remain ~8-13 mg/L through 96 h without approaching 2 mg/L
Receiving P assay at t=239 h = 3.04 g/L, consistent with source batches at same age (2.98, 3.02, 5.33 g/L range) indicating normal production
No DO dips, oscillations, or anomalies in receiving trace that would justify intervention under KEEP
args.rationale: Receiving DO at decision time (52 h) is ~10.5–10.9 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L hard limit, and its slow decline mirrors the three source batches, which never approach the limit over 96 h. Latest available receiving product assay (3.04 g/L at t=239 h of the source-referenced clock) matches source kinetics. Under KEEP, predicted DO stays well above 2 mg/L for the remaining simulated horizon; no intervention is needed, and any feed reduction or air change would only reduce product mass. Alternatives (reduce_feed, increase_air, combined, strong_feed_reduction) are unsupported: there is no evidence of oxygen deficit or over-feeding. Stop would forfeit all counted production without justification.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters differ from source; the DO decline could steepen after 52 h. However, the margin is >8 mg/L and the observed slope (~0.1 mg/L/h over recent hours, slowing) gives large headroom over any plausible remaining horizon. Forecast model mismatch risk is acknowledged; sensor noise is visible (~±0.3 mg/L) but negligible relative to the margin. If a sharp DO drop occurred, increase_air would be the fallback, but current evidence does not predict it.
